subject: Throughput & streaming qualification runbook request
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Matt Turner <matt.turner@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: quant targets & inputs we need for performance qual

Hi Matt — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can scope the qualification run: 

Summary from our call
- Target latency SLOs: 95th percentile <= 220ms for single-turn, non-streaming generation (50 tokens).
- Streaming requirement: mid-stream token rollout with 50ms early token delivery target for the first partial chunk (you mentioned using streaming in the product UI).
- Throughput: steady-state ~120 reqs/min during peak retail hours; burst to 600 reqs/min for short windows (~2-3 minutes) during flash events.
- Concurrency assumption: 200 concurrent active sessions.

What we need from your side to build the benchmark runbook and prompt/harness bundle:
1) Representative prompt set (CSV or JSONL) — include samples for short queries (10–30 tokens), medium (50 tokens), and long (200+ tokens).
2) Traffic profile: expected arrival distribution (per minute), any diurnal curve, and examples of burst patterns. A small JSON or CSV is fine.
3) Confirmation whether you will test with streaming on (true/false) and which UI behavior matters most (first-token latency vs stable throughput).
4) Any IP/data restrictions for a private harness runner (e.g., sample data must be redacted, cannot leave your VPC).

Proposed next steps
- If you can drop the prompt set and traffic_profile.json by EOD Wednesday (your timezone), Marissa will produce a first-pass runbook and an eval harness config for you to review.
- We’ll propose two benchmark runs: (A) non-streaming 95p latency sweep and (B) streaming partial-token latency + sustained throughput.

Attachment placeholders: [Attachment: sample_prompts_template.csv (CSV, 8KB)] [Attachment: traffic_profile_example.json (JSON, 3KB)]

Thanks — I’ll loop in Marissa for the runbook draft.

Best,
Irene Choi

Irene — appreciate the clear asks. Attaching a sanitized sample of our prompts and a compact traffic profile. Answers inline below.

Quick answers
- Prompt set: attached (sample_prompts.csv) — includes the 3 length buckets you requested. Some customer-facing text is redacted per policy.
- Traffic profile: attached (traffic_profile.json) — peak at 120 reqs/min, typical steady 40–60 reqs/min, burst simulation example provided (600 reqs/min for 150s).
- Streaming: yes, we plan to use streaming for product A. The first-token latency matters most for perceived responsiveness — if the first chunk takes >120ms users complain. Subsequent tokens can be amortized.
- Data restrictions: prompts are sanitized; we cannot permit leaving our VPC for PII samples. We can either run the harness in your private runner or provide container images.

Subject: draft runbook: throughput/concurrency + streaming measurement definitions (v0.1)

Hi Matt — I pulled the attachments and sketched a short runbook and measurement definitions. Attaching the markdown draft and a zipped prompt bundle for the harness. High-level notes below; full steps are in runbook_v0.1.md.

Key measurement primitives (short)
- Test harness environment: single-region US-west, identical GPU flavor (p3-equivalent) for baseline. Record CPU/memory/gpu utilization.
- Non-streaming 95p latency: issue closed requests with 50-token max; measure p50/p95/p99 over 30-minute steady windows.
- Streaming first-chunk latency: measure time from request to first chunk available to client; target for acceptance is <=120ms median and <=220ms 95p under 200 concurrent sessions.
- Throughput sweep: ramp to target steady-state (120 reqs/min) and validate sustained QPS for 15 minutes; run burst test (600 reqs/min for 180 seconds) and observe tail latencies and error rate.
- Reproducibility: each run includes a seed set of 10K prompts plus 3 fixed prompt variants flagged in prompt_bundle_v1.zip. Use deterministic temperature=0.0 config for repeatability where model supports it.

Run steps (summary)
1) Deploy harness container (we can provide or you can host).
2) Upload prompt_bundle_v1.zip and traffic_profile.json to harness.
3) Run baseline non-streaming sweep (A) and collect traces/logs.
4) Run streaming sweep (B) including first-chunk latency probes and sustained throughput window.
5) Produce CSV of per-request latencies and a consolidated run report.

Access & safe-data options
- Option 1 (preferred): we run harness on your private runner image; we supply container and config, Acme provides ephemeral credentials.
- Option 2: we run in Redwood's hosted evaluation cluster but only on fully sanitized data (not acceptable per your note).

Attachments: [Attachment: runbook_v0.1.md (Markdown, 18KB)] [Attachment: prompt_bundle_v1.zip (ZIP, 450KB)]

Can you confirm which option you prefer and a 2-hour window next week for the two benchmark runs?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
